artworks.title: The Soul of Integration
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
The Soul of Integration, 2025

A woman in profile, dark skin and a white tribal-patterned mask, wears a vibrant turban of red, white, blue and green, with colorful hands reaching toward her from a golden aura.
Around her, sacred symbols — cross, Om, crescent and star, Khanda, Jain hand, Dharma wheel — float on a golden ground alongside arched temple forms.
To her right, a vertical column of world flags — USA, India, UK, Argentina, France and others — rises above a field of white flowers.
The blue forms above, filled with fish and water, recall your earlier Water and Life — suggesting integration includes nature itself.
Curatorially, this is a synthesis painting: African tribal mask, Indian spirituality, global vexillology and folk motifs merged into one visage.
Conceptually, integration is not erasure but coexistence — the mask remains distinct, yet it holds all faiths and nations within its surrounding light.
The reaching hands symbolize humanity's universal gesture of welcome, while her serene gaze suggests soul is the true integrator, beyond religion or nationality.
It declares that the soul of integration is not uniformity, but luminous unity in diversity — many colors, one light.
artworks.artist_attribution: Signed and dated on verso by Ashok Kumar

artworks.title: A tribute to the divine souls
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
A Tribute to the Divine Souls, 2021 

A kneeling woman in a vibrant striped sari, face painted as a calavera with gold filigree and marigold flowers in her hair, offers a blue floral ofrenda pot.
She is surrounded by three ornate sugar skulls — one resting on her shoulder like a whisper, two floating nearby — each adorned with crosses and flowers.
Rendered in bold cubist planes of peach, green, red and yellow, her body is both festive and sacred.
The background of deep reds and purples suggests ritual space, not mourning.
Conceptually, death is shown not as loss but as luminous continuity — decorated, beloved, present.
The cross on each skull merges faith with ancestry, making the divine soul universal.
Marigolds and offerings ground the spiritual in everyday acts of remembrance.
It is a tribute that celebrates the dead as still dancing with us, in color and light.

artworks.title: Standing together
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Standing Together, 2016

Three figures in deep blue sit shoulder to shoulder, hands crossed in quiet unity, two in profile gazing at the centre one who faces us.
Their shared posture and identical shirts speak of solidarity — individual yet collective, distinct yet bound by a common rhythm.
Behind them, a luminous field of white and green suggests hope, while an ochre band with tribal glyphs anchors the scene in earth.
Below, a frieze of Warli-like figures, animals, fish and turtles narrates community life, tradition and coexistence with nature.
A large white orb at the bottom centre acts as a moon or mirror, reflecting the group's shared consciousness.
The deep blue border frames them like a shrine, elevating ordinary togetherness into something sacred.
Conceptually, the work is about strength in unity — not uniformity, but harmonious standing together despite difference.
It reminds us that community is both our roots below and our light above.

artworks.title: Floating within
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Floating within Peace, 2016

An orange figure sits cross-legged in meditation, eyes closed, hands forming a lotus over a golden core, enveloped by a vast white aura.
Above, a blue-green winged figure with outstretched arms hovers — its guardian spirit, its higher consciousness floating within.
Curatorially, the painting inverts inside and outside: the inner peace is huge, the outer world — dark glyphs above and below — is reduced to a thin edge.
Conceptually, true floating is not escape from the body but inhabiting it fully, where self and soul meet in stillness.
It shows peace not as quiet surroundings, but as a luminous space we carry and expand within us.

artworks.title: Water and Life
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
This is "Water and Life" — a celebration of water as the source.

A vibrant ocean of turquoise, blue and green swirls with golden fish, shrimp, a turtle and sun-like creatures dancing around a bold red fish at the centre.
The red fish anchors the composition, connected by a thin lifeline to the abstract world below, suggesting life depends on water.
Golden and ochre aquatic forms move in rhythm, creating energy, abundance and the interconnectedness of all water life.
Small symbols — a cross, triangle and sun — float in the water, hinting at faith, nature and cosmos within this ecosystem.
Below, a calm, geometric landscape in blues and greens holds two dark and green circles, like reflections or eyes watching over the balance.
Together, the painting speaks of purity, movement and continuity — where water holds, nourishes and sustains life itself.

artworks.title: Inside Expression
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Two masks in dialogue — a red frontal face smiling outward, and a yellow crescent profile gazing inward, like sun and moon.
They rest on a dense field of invented glyphs in ochre, white and maroon, an undeciphered script of culture and memory.
A pale border of soft totemic symbols — crosses, circles, trees — frames them like silent witnesses at the edge of mind.
The red mask is the social self we show the world; the yellow is the inner self that watches and dreams.
Overlapping yet distinct, they embody the duality of identity — the outer performance and the inner truth.
The chaotic script behind is the noise of society, language and history that conditions our expression.
Yet the masks remain clear and luminous, suggesting authentic selfhood endures within that noise.
The painting asks: when we express, who is speaking — the face we wear, or the quiet moon living inside?

artworks.title: Essence of Joy
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Two figures embrace in a field of intense red — a woman in warm yellow gazing outward, a man in tranquil green gazing at her.
Their simplified forms overlap, colors bleeding into each other, suggesting unity rather than separation.
Behind them, dark fragmented glyphs like a chaotic city contrast the calm of their closeness.
Above, a burst of white and yellow light breaks through like a blessing.
Joy here is not laughter, but stillness — the quiet fullness of being seen and seeing in return.
Kumar shows love as environment, not event — a vital space that holds us against worldly noise.
Masculine and feminine appear as balanced energies, equal and complementary, not dominant.
The essence is presence itself — to remain luminous together while darkness flickers behind.

Dream Golden, 2015

A serene blue-green bust with closed eyes emerges from darkness below, while a luminous golden-yellow translucent figure with a cross on its face stands above it, like an aura.
Flanked by vertical bands of intense red marked with golden glyphs, the composition places the spiritual between the material and the sacred.
Curatorially, it is a double portrait of the self — the grounded meditator and the illuminated higher self hovering above.
Conceptually, the golden dream is enlightenment itself — the moment when inner stillness births a radiant, weightless identity beyond ego.
The painting says our dreams are not outside us; they are our larger, golden selves waiting to be remembered.

Conceptually, imagination is portrayed not as escape but as inward incubation — the pause where outer reality softens and inner vision takes shape.

A green-hued male figure stands meditative at top left, eyes closed, surrounded by seven white butterflies and one black — duality and transformation hovering like thoughts.

Conceptually, cosmic consciousness is not ascent but awareness of this duality — where butterflies of the mind float, and the soul watches itself becoming.

artworks.title: Echoes of a Bygone Era
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Title: Echoes of a Bygone Era

Medium: Watercolour on Paper
Curatorial Description
Echoes of a Bygone Era captures the imposing presence of an old steam locomotive, presenting a compelling study of industrial heritage, time, and memory. Through a close-up composition, the artist draws attention to the intricate mechanical structure, massive iron wheels, connecting rods, weathered surfaces, and traces of rust that define the locomotive's character.

The contrast between the deep, dark tones of the engine and the soft earthy colours of the surrounding landscape creates a striking visual relationship between industrial strength and the quiet passage of nature. Delicate watercolour washes, layered tonal variations, and expressive brushwork bring out the textures of metal, rust, grass, and weathered machinery.

Rather than depicting the locomotive simply as a machine, the artist presents it as a silent witness to another era—an object carrying the memories of journeys, human labour, technological progress, and changing landscapes.
Conceptual Essay
The painting explores the relationship between industrial history, the passage of time, and the persistence of memory. Once symbols of speed, progress, and modern civilisation, steam locomotives transformed transportation and connected distant places, people, and cultures. Today, many of these magnificent machines have become remnants of a fading industrial age.

Through this artwork, the artist reflects on the beauty of ageing and the emotional significance of forgotten objects. The weathered metal, rusted components, and monumental wheels suggest not merely physical decay but the accumulated stories of countless journeys. The locomotive appears frozen in time, yet its powerful presence evokes movement, sound, labour, and life.

The surrounding vegetation offers another layer of meaning. Nature gradually reclaiming the railway environment symbolises the inevitable cycle of change, where human creations eventually become part of the natural world. The contrast between the mechanical structure and the organic landscape creates a quiet dialogue between civilisation and nature.

Watercolour is particularly suited to expressing this subject. Its transparency, fluidity, and delicate tonal transitions allow the artist to balance the solidity of industrial machinery with the atmospheric softness of the surrounding environment.

Ultimately, Echoes of a Bygone Era is a reflection on nostalgia, impermanence, and the passage of time. It invites viewers to look beyond the physical structure of an old locomotive and recognise it as a vessel of collective memory—a reminder of an age when machines carried not only passengers and goods but also the dreams and aspirations of generations.

Artist's Statement:

Through this painting, I seek to preserve the visual and emotional presence of an industrial past. I am fascinated by the textures, forms, and stories embedded in ageing machinery. My intention is to transform an ordinary industrial object into a subject of artistic contemplation, where history, memory, and nature come together in a quiet visual narrative.

artworks.title: Rhythmic Symbols
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Rhythmic Symbols, 2012 - Acrylic on Canvas

A vibrant abstract where undulating turquoise, green and cobalt forms flow like a melodic wave across a warm ground of ochre, gold and sand.
A central vertical spine anchors the flux - layered with geometric glyphs, tribal totems and calligraphic marks in red, brown and black.
The work visualizes rhythm as color-pulse - cool, fluid movements punctuated by sharp whites, blues and earthy interruptions.
Conceptually, it explores language before language - symbols that feel like a forgotten alphabet, half-remembered from dream, ritual and folk memory.
The fluid, airy top and grounded, earthy bottom suggest a dialogue between sky-mind and earth-body, conscious and subconscious.
The stylized figures are not figures, but markers of human presence in abstraction - repetition as ritual, rhythm as meaning.
In its joyous palette and syncopated structure, the painting becomes a visual raga - improvisational, yet held by an inner order.
It asks not to be decoded, but felt - to let color, shape and symbol resonate like music.

artworks.title: Cosmic symbols
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Cosmic Symbols, 2012 - Acrylic on Canvas

A vertical cosmology in three registers: an ethereal turquoise field holding the Om at center, a mediating blue orb in a dark triangle, and a warm earth-grid below.
The Om anchors the upper akasha, surrounded by faint crosses and runic fragments - the sacred as a frequency in a field of blue-green light.
The central bindu - a dense, textured cobalt circle - acts as portal, sun, and eye, suspended between the celestial and the terrestrial.
Below, a mandala of ochre and gold tablets unfolds, each incised with proto-scripts, spirals, and sigils - like Indus seals reimagined for the cosmos.
Conceptually, the work maps the journey of sound to symbol to matter - from Pranava to planet, from mantra to math, from infinity to inscription.
It proposes that all writing systems are fragments of one cosmic script, a universal grammar that connects Vedic, tribal and futuristic signs.
The cool blues of spirit and warm ochres of earth are not opposed, but in constant translation through the central sphere of consciousness.
A visual Upanishad - where the artist suggests the universe itself is a text, and every symbol is a star trying to be read.

artworks.title: Ocean Symbols
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Ocean Symbols, 2012- Acrylic on Canvas

A luminous seascape of mind, where a deep, flowing blue biomorph cradles four golden tablets against a sun-washed yellow horizon.
Three symbols float in alignment, the fourth descending below - like a tide of language, with one glyph breaking off, sinking, returning to depth.
The background breathes in washes of aquamarine, turquoise and green, evoking water, sky and memory merging into one fluid field.
The glyphs - fish, figure, loop, and angular vessel - are not letters but aquatic archetypes, fossils of a script born in the ocean.
Conceptually, the work posits the ocean as the first archive, where life and language emerged together in salt and symbol.
It suggests myths travel like currents - the Matsya, the ancient fish, reappears here as a pictograph adrift on a sea of color.
In its bold, almost childlike simplicity, the painting balances abstraction and totem - vastness held within intimate, sacred squares.
A meditation on what remains when the tide recedes: not words, but the elemental signs that still remember water.

artworks.title: Mask
artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Mask, 2017 - Acrylic on Canvas, 33 x 24 in

Two seated figures, rendered in flat, tender hues of ivory and vermilion, cradle a dark, ancestral mask between them against a fractured landscape.
The mask is the chromatic and spiritual anchor - heavy, olive-black, timeless - held gently, not worn, as if in dialogue, offering, or interrogation.
Behind, a dynamic field of blue peaks, ochre shards, and crystalline white facets erupts, suggesting both Himalayan memory and cubist fragmentation.
The figures wear their own faces like masks - serene, painted, simplified - blurring the line between self and artifact, wearer and worn.
Conceptually, the painting questions inheritance: what we hold from our ancestors, what we choose to carry, and what carries us.
The mask is not concealment, but lineage - an object of power that requires two to hold, a collective negotiation of identity.
In its warm earth tones and sharp geometric light, the work becomes a parable of modern duality: innocence confronting archetype.
A quiet, deeply human ritual - to look into the face of the past without hiding one's own.

artworks.provenance: Direct from the studio of the artist.
artworks.description:
Destined Origin East and West, 2016 - Acrylic on Canvas

Two luminous yellow ovals, like twin suns or worlds, are joined by a grey band of ancient scripts, holding a vivid blue paper boat at its center.
Around the vessel orbit wooden archetypes: a maternal figure and shark on the West, a standing fetish, mask, turtle and hornbill on the East.
The composition is a cartography of migration - not of continents, but of symbols, myths and totems adrift between shores.
The origami boat is the hinge: fragile, modern, geometric, yet carrying the weight of ancestral wood across a sea of language.
Conceptually, the work argues there is no pure East or West, only a destined shared origin, where African, Oceanic and Indian forms converse.
The turtle below grounds the myth in earth-time, while the boat points to childlike possibility, to journeys yet to be folded.
Painted in warm ochres, cool greys and sharp primaries, it collapses anthropology into poetry, archive into dream.
A visual sutra of cultural confluence - we have always been sailing towards each other, on the same paper ocean.

artist_profiles.biography: Contemporary visual artist represented on ArtAlly.
I'm based on indian fine art and commercial photographer, I studied in bachelor of fine arts in photography in andhara pradesh

Delving into the depths of cultural diversity and human imagination, Ashok Kumar's artistic journey transcends borders, weaving together threads of inspiration from France to New Delhi, India. Born on February 1st, 1965, in the vibrant landscapes of Bihar, India, Kumar's artistic odyssey began at the College of Art, Patna, where he emerged as a beacon of creativity, graduating with distinction in 1987.
Fuelled by a relentless pursuit of artistic excellence, Kumar embarked on a transformative voyage of learning, securing a coveted scholarship for advanced studies in fine art at “L’Ecole Superieure des Beaux-arts de Marseille, France”, in 1990. His dedication and talent were further recognized with a prestigious senior fellowship in painting from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in 2015-16, a testament to his enduring commitment to his craft.
Kumar's artistic repertoire is a kaleidoscope of imagery, a symphony of symbols and signs that speak to the human experience and our intrinsic connection to nature. Through his mesmerizing creations, he invites viewers into a realm of heightened consciousness and spirituality, where semi-figurative forms intertwine harmoniously with the organic world, evoking a sense of wonder and awe. A true global citizen of the art world, Kumar's work has traversed continents, leaving an indelible mark on audiences from France to Peru, from China to Chile, and beyond. His participation in major national and international workshops, festivals, art residencies, and exhibitions has earned him acclaim and admiration worldwide. Notably, his art has graced the prestigious ARTSY PAGE by ACS Gallery, Chicago, USA, in 2017, captivating audiences with its profound beauty and depth.
In the ever-evolving landscape of contemporary art, Kumar remains steadfast in his commitment to uplifting the cultural heritage of India while embracing the universal language of creativity. His presence in numerous international art exhibitions from 2020 to 2026 underscores his unwavering dedication to sharing his vision with the world. To experience the trans-formative power of Ashok Kumar's art is to embark on a journey of enlightenment and introspection, where boundaries dissolve, and the essence of humanity shines forth.

Artistic Statement
My creation explores new vision through the imagination of the human being as an origin belongs to our cultural diversity with many symbols and signs. What we indulge or experience in the surrounding nature with positive vibes and thoughts are usually creating ecstasy in our mind and radiates peace with togetherness. I depict aesthetically the semi-figurative human form with the relevant combination of nature and other organisms in my creation to explore the high consciousness and spirituality.
